steps.title: Prepare glass window construct
steps.instruction: Position a custom steel ring upside down, apply a small amount of optical adhesive NOA 68 (Norland Products, catalog 25882E) to the bottom rim using a paper point, place a 3 mm Ø #0 thickness cover glass (Warner Instruments, catalog 64‑0726) on the adhesive, press gently with forceps to eliminate air gaps, then cure under a 100 W UV lamp for 3 min.

steps.title: Prepare ground wire construct
steps.instruction: Cut silver wire (Advent, catalog AG549311) to ~3 cm, strip the Teflon coating, remove plastic from the PCB pin and trim the end; optionally loop both ends and solder onto the pin for stability, chlorinate the tip in bleach for a few minutes, rinse thoroughly with demi‑water.

steps.title: Induce anesthesia and pre‑operative analgesia
steps.instruction: Induce anesthesia with isoflurane at ~0.8 L/min, 5% until unconscious, then place the mouse under a face mask on a heating pad and maintain ~0.8 L/min, 2% isoflurane, adjusting as needed; apply eye ointment (Alcon Duratears Z, catalog 10308); inject carprofen 5 mg/kg SC (ASTfarma Carporal 50 mg/mL) and buprenorphine 0.05 mg/kg SC (Dechra Bupredine Multidose 0.3 mg/mL); if a cranial window will be made, inject 15 % D‑mannitol (Sigma, catalog M4125‑100g) at 2 000 mg/kg IP.

steps.title: Expose scalp and clean skull
steps.instruction: Straighten the head using a roll of paper tissue or ear bars, wet the fur with lidocaine spray (Aspen Xylocaine spray, 100 mg/mL) and shave the scalp with a scalpel, avoiding the nose; sterilize skin with 70 % ethanol, spray lidocaine on a clean scalpel and make a skin incision from 1–2 mm caudal to the occipital ridge to the middle of the two eyes; spray additional lidocaine on the incision site and exposed periosteum, pull skin laterally, cut periosteum along the incision perimeter, locate Bregma and Lambda, make a small midline incision caudally to separate thin dorsal neck muscles, push muscles laterally to expose the occipital ridge and attached splenius/semispinalis capitis muscles, detach these muscles from the occipital bone with fine scissors or forceps, scratch the bone with a curette or scalpel tip to remove remaining periosteum and muscle, clean the exposed skull with 70 % ethanol, let air‑dry briefly, and insert four paper points between the occipital bone, skin and underneath the muscle on the interparietal bone.

steps.title: Etch and prime skull surface
steps.instruction: Apply dental etching gel (Etch Rite, 38 % phosphoric acid, Pulpdent, catalog 185120) to the skull and let it sit for 15–30 s until the surface becomes matte, then wipe away the gel with a cotton swab wetted with 0.9 % NaCl saline (Baxter, catalog TKF7124) until no residue remains; apply bonding primer OptiBond FL 1 Prime (Kerr, catalog 25881E) with a micro applicator and let air‑dry (no excess, slight shine), then apply bonding adhesive OptiBond FL 2 Adhesive (Kerr, catalog 25882E) over the entire exposed skull using a scratching motion while applying pressure, and cure the adhesive with UV light as per manufacturer’s specifications.

steps.title: Attach headplate with adhesive and composite
steps.instruction: Apply OptiBond FL 2 adhesive to the underside of the clean round headplate (in‑house, 1 mm thick, 10 mm outer ring, 7 mm inner ring, 18 mm wing‑to‑wing, ~500 mg), position it on the skull so the opening lies slightly caudal to Lambda and the plate contacts the bone as closely as possible, cure the headplate‑bone bond with UV light while preventing movement, then secure the headplate with dental composite (Charisma A1, Heraeus, catalog 66056076; optionally flowable Charisma Flow A1, catalog 66015495) filling all gaps, ensuring solid contact with the occipital bone and the parietal/interparietal bones, fill the rostral skull area with composite without excess that would increase imaging distance, and finally attach any loose skin to the caudal side of the headplate using superglue (UHU, catalog 62687).

substeps.instruction: Optional pause: if the craniotomy will be performed in a later surgery, apply and UV‑cure a thin layer of flowable dental composite on the exposed skull to protect the bone before proceeding to recovery.

steps.title: Perform craniotomy (thin skull)
steps.instruction: Using a fine drill (Ø 0.3 mm, Komet Dental, catalog H71 104 003), locate the inferior colliculus (IC) region with atlas coordinates, sequentially thin the skull while removing debris; after the vascular middle layer is removed, apply saline so the bone becomes transparent and mildly flexible, continue thinning until membranous, adding an extra margin of ~0.3 mm at the surface to accommodate the window, rinse with saline, ensure hemostasis, then, with fine forceps, carefully chip away the remaining bone from the cerebellum side until the IC is visible (white, shiny) and the dura remains intact.

steps.title: Variant 1: Install cranial window for imaging
steps.instruction: Fit a pre‑prepared steel‑ring cranial window (≈10 mm × 15 mm metal loop, covered with tape or hard plastic ≈70 mm²) into the craniotomy, expanding the opening if necessary while avoiding bone shards; apply a tiny drop of superglue (UHU, catalog 62687) at 2–3 contact points between the window rim and bone, then secure the window with dental adhesive or cement, applying firm pressure to prevent connective‑tissue growth (rule of thumb: if it feels pressed enough, it is sufficient); optionally fasten the entire window with superglue for a removable configuration, and close the headplate lid once the glue has dried.

steps.title: Variant 2: Prepare craniotomy for electrophysiology
steps.instruction: Apply OptiBond FL 1 primer to the edges of the craniotomy with a paper point and let it air‑dry briefly, then apply OptiBond FL 2 adhesive to the craniotomy funnel and cure with UV light; create a well of dental composite around the craniotomy and cure with UV; secure the ground pin (prepared earlier) outside or on the edge of the headplate using Charisma composite, gently slide the chlorinated silver wire between brain and skull, fill the well with silicone gel sealant (Dura‑Gel, Cambridge NeuroTech, catalog Dura‑Gel or DOWSIL 3‑4680, catalog 3‑4680), remove bubbles with fine forceps, and allow the gel to set for 30 min; then secure the ground construct with additional dental composite, leaving the pin opening exposed, form a sheet of composite covering the ground construct and the remaining exposed skull, and make a protective cover by looping wire around the headplate wings.

steps.title: Post‑operative recovery
steps.instruction: If 15 % D‑mannitol was injected, follow with an equal volume of 0.9 % NaCl saline IP; stop isoflurane and allow the mouse to awaken, waiting for the first spontaneous movements, then transfer the animal to its home cage under a heat lamp or heating pad; for electrophysiology recordings, allow 3–4 days of recovery before awake experiments, and for two‑photon calcium imaging allow 3–4 days (minimum) and preferably two weeks for stable long‑term recordings.
